safety_tips.tip: Keep your belongings secure, especially in crowded areas like stations and tourist attractions.
Avoid displaying valuables openly such as phones, wallets, and passports.
Stay alert in busy public transport areas, particularly in Paris.
Use crossbody or anti-theft bags where possible.
Stick to well-lit areas at night.
Be mindful of belongings in metro stations and while boarding trains.
Avoid street scams such as petition signers and distraction tactics near landmarks.
Use official taxis or public transport.
Keep valuables secure in crowded tourist areas, metro stations, and train platforms.
Avoid keeping phones or wallets loosely in jacket pockets while sightseeing.
Use official taxis or trusted ride apps where available.
Be extra mindful around busy tourist attractions, especially in Paris, Rome, and Venice.
Carry a mix of cards and limited cash instead of large amounts of currency.
Keep digital and printed copies of passports, visas, insurance, and bookings.
Always monitor your luggage carefully during train travel and station transfers.

connectivity_tips.tip: eSIMs are the easiest connectivity option — no physical SIM required and can be activated before departure via QR code. Popular providers include Airalo, Nomad, and Holafly, with Europe-wide coverage including France and Switzerland.

Local SIM card providers in France include Orange France (strong coverage, tourist-friendly plans), SFR (good speeds and availability), and Bouygues Telecom (popular among travelers). Available at convenience stores and official telecom shops. Passport required.
Paris has excellent 4G/5G coverage across the city, metro, and tourist areas.
Strong connectivity on most train routes; brief signal drops in tunnels are normal.
Wi-Fi is widely available in hotels, cafés, and stations throughout France and Switzerland.

eSIM is recommended for convenience — activate before leaving India. Popular providers include Airalo, Nomad, and Holafly. Purchase online, scan QR code, and activate instantly with no physical SIM needed. Choose a Europe-wide plan if traveling beyond Switzerland.

International roaming from India is the most effortless option but usually more expensive. Popular providers: Airtel International Roaming and Jio International Packs. Check data limits carefully as plans can be costly.
Download Google Maps offline for all destinations before traveling.

An eSIM is the easiest and most convenient option for multi-country Europe trips. Recommended providers: Airalo, Holafly, Nomad. Works across multiple European countries with no physical SIM swapping required.

Local SIM cards available from Orange, SFR, and Bouygues Telecom. Purchase at Charles de Gaulle Airport, Gare du Nord station, telecom stores, or supermarkets. Passport usually required for SIM registration. Excellent coverage across Paris and most tourist areas.

health_tips.tip: No special or mandatory vaccinations are required for Indian travelers visiting France or Switzerland.
Tap water is safe to drink in Switzerland and most parts of Paris.
Vegetarian food is widely available — opt for well-reviewed restaurants for best quality.
Temperatures can vary significantly, especially in the mountains — dress in layers to avoid catching a cold.
Use moisturizers, sunscreen (SPF 50 recommended), and sunglasses — cold air can be drying and snow glare can be strong.

Carry a basic medical kit including fever, cold, and flu medication; digestion tablets; motion sickness medication for mountain routes; band-aids and basic first-aid; and any personal prescription medicines with a copy of the prescription.
Nearest medical facility to Voco Paris – Porte de Clichy: Health Center Hospital Goüin, approximately 10 minutes walk, open 9 AM–8 PM.
Tap water is safe to drink across all cities and mountain regions — carry a reusable bottle to stay hydrated.
Carry basic medications including personal prescriptions, cold & flu relief, motion sickness tablets, and a small first-aid kit.
Travel insurance is highly recommended to cover medical needs, delays, or unforeseen situations during your trip.
No special vaccinations are mandatory for Indian travellers visiting France, Switzerland, and Italy for tourism.
Recommended vaccinations: Routine vaccinations (MMR, Tetanus, Flu), Hepatitis A, and Typhoid (especially for frequent international travellers).
Stay well hydrated during sightseeing and long train journeys.
Wear comfortable walking shoes as most European cities involve extensive walking on cobblestone streets.
Use sunscreen, sunglasses, and a cap during sunny afternoons.
Carry personal medications along with a small basic first-aid kit.
Inform restaurants clearly about dietary preferences while ordering meals.
Pace sightseeing comfortably and allow adequate rest between long travel days.
Carry a small mosquito repellent and hand sanitiser for added comfort during travel.
Nearest hospital to Paris hotel: Lariboisière Hospital AP-HP, approx. 10 mins walk, open 24/7.
